method: Arrival-state maker simulation: at order arrival (decision time plus sampled latency) replay the target book to decide accepted, post-only rejected or resting, for explicit GTX at a fixed price and for exchange-side QUEUE price match
data_held: Needs M430 and M431 to survive first; the raw tape in data/rawtape (arrival-ordered target book and trades).
note: Do not reuse M427. Chasing with amended futures orders loses queue priority (charge it); model cancel latency separately from entry latency. Objective is expected value per submitted order: P(fill) x (markout given fill + spread captured - maker fee - exit cost) minus cancel-race and inventory risk, with the standard USDC maker rate and any RPI rate kept apart. Report signals, order opportunities, accept/reject rate, fill rate, fill-conditioned markout and non-fill opportunity cost, with independent hourly blocks as prominent as fills. The fill model must exclude Binance RPI size for API takers and include Bybit RPI size only when rpiTakerAccess is on. Albers et al. (Quantitative Finance 25(6), 2025; abstract read, body not) report that live market orders fill worse than the book snapshot implies and that marketable limit orders can fail to fill, so the simulator is fitted to live-order evidence before it is trusted; that needs calibration orders, which are the owner's call (rule 5). Targeted check 2026-10-28: (1) design hurdle, a new hypothesis rather than a result: a quoting rule earns a fill model only if its fill-conditioned markout beats the markout of simply joining the touch at the same moments, by more than exit cost and the maker fee; the touch-join baseline is estimated from our own tape, not taken from a paper (the pasted 125-million-fill figures of -0.39/-0.84/-0.46 bp are now located, see the correction below, and are still not used as a hurdle). Located literature pointing the same way, search summaries only: arXiv 2608.18195 (best-price fills cost about half a tick in a stable simulated market) and arXiv 2502.18625 (live Binance, 232,897 minimum maker orders, top-of-queue fills tend to precede adverse moves). (2) Venue rule: Binance's invalid cancellation ratio counts any GTC/RPI/GTX/GTD order cancelled under 5 s; it binds at 0.99 over at least 5,000 orders per symbol per 10 minutes, so the simulator reports its own sub-5 s cancel share per symbol per cycle. (3) The pasted EV form EV(bid) = P(fill | X) [cross-venue alpha + forced-flow alpha - toxicity + spread - cost] is this row's objective with two named terms; each alpha term is a separate lane (M430, M434, M435) and enters only after it survives alone. Correction 2026-10-28 (the earlier 'not found' was wrong): the figures are Gatto, SSRN 7461901, seen only in search results because SSRN returns 403 from this container, so the body and method were not read. They describe about 125.8 million SIMULATED last-in-queue fills with 10 s markouts before fees of -0.839 bp on Bybit, -0.391 on Binance and -0.458 on Hyperliquid, for the entry leg only. Simulated and last-in-queue means a pessimistic bound for joining the back of the queue, not a measurement of real fills and not a verdict on resting at the touch in general; it is a reason to test, not a number to net against. Reporting rule (owner's third review): every simulated fill result is shown under three allocations of unobserved cancels, back-cancel (every cancel is behind us, so our position never improves from cancels: pessimistic), random-cancel (uniform over the queue: central) and front-cancel (every cancel is ahead of us: optimistic), each with fill probability, fill-conditioned markout and expected value per submitted order with intervals over independent hourly blocks. A rule is promoted only if the pessimistic and the central constructions are both positive net of the ordinary maker fee; the optimistic one alone never promotes. M437 supplies exact cancels by order uid on Kraken, so it measures how far the three L2-based allocations are from the truth there. Primary target (owner's form): EV_quote(X) = P(fill|X) [spread + E(markout|fill,X) + rebate - maker fee - exit cost] - inventory risk - cancel-race risk - tail risk, and the model may answer NO QUOTE; no deep model until simple components show out-of-sample value.
